# PEAK Game Wiki: Complete Site Guide

> PEAK Game Wiki is an independent multilingual reference prototype for the Steam co-op climbing game PEAK. It organizes practical map, equipment, progress, multiplayer, and update questions into a source-aware homepage. It is not an official developer site and does not host the game or provide a browser-playable version.

## Site Background

The project exists because PEAK questions arrive in several forms at once. A player may search for a daily map, then immediately need to know whether a piton or food item is worth a slot, how many people can join, or whether a recent patch changed a route hazard. A useful wiki should connect those questions instead of treating them as isolated keyword pages.

The first release is intentionally small. The homepage leads with a map-rotation desk, a version desk, a searchable prototype item index, a progress-tracking model, co-op field notes, and FAQ answers. Exact item effects, drop locations, live route results, and definitive achievement conditions require a maintained source table before they are published as final facts.

Official Steam store information, Steam screenshots, and Steam news posts are the primary sources for game facts, official update names, dates, player-count statements, and visual context. Practical advice is presented as a field note when it is based on gameplay reasoning rather than a first-party statement. The project does not claim affiliation with Landfall or the PEAK developers. Version-sensitive information should be checked against the game and official news feed after every update.

## Content Category Details

### Map Rotation Desk (https://peak-game.wiki/)

The map section is a planning entry point, not a fabricated live tracker. It explains that PEAK uses a changing map rotation and gives players a short checklist: confirm the active route in-game, pack around the expected hazard, and log the result for future attempts. Dated history is added only when a stable maintenance source verifies it.

### PEAK Map Rotation Guide (https://peak-game.wiki/map-rotation)

The map rotation guide separates the evergreen informational intent of `PEAK map rotation` from the time-sensitive navigation intent of `PEAK map today`. It explains how to verify the active route in-game, plan rope, piton, food, and recovery utility, distinguish biomes from route stages, and record version-aware field notes. It does not invent a live biome result or publish an unsupported fixed map schedule.

### PEAK Biomes List (https://peak-game.wiki/peak-biomes-list)

The PEAK biomes list records the current source-backed roster: Shore, Tropics, Roots, Alpine, Mesa, Caldera, The Kiln, Gloom, and Citadel. It distinguishes a biome label from a map, route, stage, or local landmark, then gives cautious terrain-reading and team-planning notes. The page includes a build-time daily map entry linked to the canonical map rotation page. Exact hazards, item effects, and fixed layouts remain subject to the current game and official updates.

### PEAK Game Update Log (https://peak-game.wiki/peak-game-update)

The PEAK game update log records confirmed official Steam update titles and dates, including patch notes, content announcements, The Final Ascent, and biome updates. Its build-time table preserves official titles and links to the first-party news feed while using cautious summaries instead of inventing untranscribed mechanics. The page places today's map at the top, explains how an update can affect route context without proving a daily sequence, and links to the rotation schedule and beginner guide.

### PEAK Achievements Guide (https://peak-game.wiki/achievements)

The achievements guide targets the informational intent behind `PEAK achievements`, `PEAK achievement guide`, and `how to get all PEAK achievements`. It treats Steam achievements as platform progress and in-game badges as a separate system, then gives players a checklist method for exact names, route or mode, team members, evidence, and version. It also explains why custom runs, hidden achievements, new achievements, and missing unlocks should be verified against the current game and official Steam pages instead of being presented as permanent facts.

### Item Database (https://peak-game.wiki/)

The item section separates gear, food, and utility categories and provides browser-side search and filters. The current entries are concise field-note stubs for Piton, Anti-Rope Cannon, Bugle of Friendship, Energy Drink, Portable Stove, and Backpack. The page explicitly labels this as prototype data rather than claiming complete effects or drop tables.

### Version Desk (https://peak-game.wiki/)

The updates section highlights Patch Notes 2.03.a, the Gloom and Citadel announcement, and Patch 2.02.a from August 2026. Each note is framed as an update anchor that should connect to affected map, item, hazard, and progress pages. The official Steam news feed is linked for the complete source post.

### Progress And Co-op Notes (https://peak-game.wiki/#guides)

The progress model distinguishes Steam achievements from in-game badges and cosmetic context. The co-op notes focus on repeated player decisions: scouting before spending stamina, sharing utility across the group, and separating official facts from practical advice. The FAQ covers solo play, group size, crossplay verification, and update freshness.

## User Value

The site helps a player decide what to check before a climb, where to start when a patch has just landed, and how to interpret PEAK vocabulary across maps, items, badges, and achievements. Its most important limitation is deliberate: it does not invent real-time map results or unsupported numerical data merely to make the page look complete. A production version should add maintained entity pages, dated route archives, Chinese localization, and stronger source-to-entry links before it expands the database.

## Latest Update Content

### Patch Notes 2.03.a (https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3527290)

The maintained update data records Patch Notes 2.03.a on 27 August 2026 as the latest confirmed official entry. The official Steam news post is the authority for exact mechanics and implementation details.

### ONE MORE WEEK OF GLOOM + THE CITADEL (https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3527290)

The maintained update data records this official content announcement on 24 August 2026. It is useful route context for players checking the current map, but its title alone does not prove the sequence in every lobby or future reset.

### PATCH 2.02.a (https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3527290)

The maintained update data records PATCH 2.02.a on 18 August 2026. As with the other entries, the log reports the confirmed title and date without inventing patch details that are not transcribed from the first-party post.

### What Is PEAK? (https://peak-game.wiki/what-is-peak-game)

The beginner guide explains PEAK as a Steam co-op climbing and survival game, using the official store page for platform, modes, and the group-size statement. It separates maps, routes, and biome labels, explains the build-time daily map entry, and gives a practical first-run loop: confirm the session, scout before spending utility, assign shared resources, choose a pause point, and record a dated observation. Advice is labeled as practical guidance rather than a permanent game rule. The guide links to the daily map page, the biomes list, and the update log, while the official Steam page remains the authority for current platform and game information.
